outcome: Early complications (surgical site infection, wound dehiscence, urinary tract infection)
Late complications (urinary dribbling/poor stream, faecal soiling)
cohort: The cohort consisted of 21 infants and children (M:F=1:3.2) diagnosed with sacrococcygeal teratoma, with a median age of 40 days (range: 1 day to 5.8 years) at presentation.
finding: Most sacrococcygeal tumors are benign, but malignancy incidence increases with age, and patients frequently experience persistent morbidities such as urinary complications (23.8%) and faecal incontinence (14.2%).
cross-section timing: Data collected between May 2023 and April 2024.
